newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli dollar-linked bonds end sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli dollar-linked bonds end sharply higher.

text.p: Prices of Israeli dollar-linked bonds rose a sharp 1.43 percent on Thursday on the back of the U.S. currency's advance on the shekel, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.03 pct to 107.1
Volume including Makams was 184 million shekels. Turnover in dollar-linked bonds was a high 23 million shekels.

"Everything was affected by the dollar," said Tiki Haddad of IBI Investment House. "Dollar-linked bonds rose sharply accompanied by sharp price rises in CPI-linked bonds on fears that the high dollar will boost inflation."
"There is a lot of uncertainty in the market and people don't really know what to do," Haddad said.
The shekel tumbled 1.5 percent against the dollar on Thursday and its representative rate was fixed at 3.5800 shekels against 3.5240 on Wednesday.

The shekel has fallen by 4.7 percent since last Friday, shortly after the government announced a reform of the exchange rate regime and the Bank of Israel lowered the base rate by a steep 1.2 percentage points to 12.7 percent.
"Trading was mixed in unlinked bonds because there are differing opinions in the market," said Ronen Elgali of United Mizrahi Bank.

"On the one hand there was a cut in interest rates, which increases the attractiveness of unlinked bonds and CPI-linked long bonds. On the other hand the rise of the dollar boosts inflation, which causes some to fear interest rates will not go down further," Elgali said.

Haddad said some traders had already started looking to buy unlinked bonds on the assumption that the central bank would intervene in the foreign exchage market to stop an excessive appreciation of the dollar.
"The central bank won't abandon its inflation target so easily," she said. "There will not be a burst of inflation."
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
